claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast condition.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
A 20–50 μm alumina-based coating deposited by pack cementation or PVD will significantly improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed intervention may instead use an alumina or silicide-based protective topcoat.
The coating will preserve room-temperature and high-temperature mechanical performance.
The topcoat will produce a dense, adherent external oxide layer.
An Al2O3 or similar external oxide barrier is thermodynamically stable and can provide oxidation resistance.
The external oxide barrier will inhibit oxygen diffusion into equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will avoid formation of non-protective, pest-prone oxide scales.
Oxidation can severely degrade the mechanical properties of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Coated specimens will show lower mass gain than uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Coated specimens will show shallower oxide penetration than uncoated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Limiting interfacial embrittlement will retain ductility and elevated-temperature strength.
Uncoated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr suffers severe oxidation damage and embrittlement in air above approximately 800 °C.
The coating is expected to be effective during approximately 5 h air exposures at 800–1000 °C.
Coating durability at higher temperatures or longer exposure times is unverified, and delamination may occur.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis specifies an alumina-based coating, whereas the intervention permits either alumina or a chemically and mechanistically distinct silicide-based topcoat; it therefore does not define a single intervention.

The conditions prescribe exposure for at least 5 h, which permits substantially longer tests, while the boundary limits the claimed effectiveness to short-term exposures of approximately 5 h and states that prolonged exposure remains unverified.
